findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md:116-122 — Workstream A permits removing the DONE-required phase deadline and relying only on per-command deadlines, but the subordinate done-prepare heartbeat contract requires every heartbeating phase to have an independent hard wall-clock deadline. Per-command timeouts do not bound orchestration hangs before, between, or after child commands. Keep a derived phase deadline (sum of effective sequential command deadlines plus bounded orchestration grace), or explicitly split the phase into mechanically bounded substeps before allowing removal. Severity: medium.

docs/requirements/decisions/workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md:293-336,417-428 — Workstream D calls the canonical owner-session contract unfinished and lists only role-separation review before implementation. The adopted session-ownership source says B-9089 already implemented the host-neutral contract, while owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:358-381 mandates fresh independent two-host PASS evidence bound to the document version before any runtime implementation. Reframe D as a regression/adapter-gap correction against shipped behavior and add the mandatory two-host review as an explicit blocking dependency and acceptance artifact; otherwise the execution plan can launch redundant or noncompliant identity work. Severity: medium.

docs/requirements/decisions/workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md:119-122 treats removing the DONE-required phase deadline as an equally valid implementation choice, but the cited canonical heartbeat plan requires every heartbeating closure phase to retain an independent hard wall-clock deadline (done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:186-190). Because section 4 says canonical subsystem documents win, this branch is not implementation-ready as written: either select the sum(effective sequential deadlines)+bounded grace design, or explicitly require updating/superseding the canonical deadline contract before removal. Severity medium: an implementer following option one can violate the current fail-closed liveness policy.

docs/requirements/decisions/workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md:297 says Workstream D will complete unfinished slices of the canonical owner-session contract, but session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:5-15 records the rollout as fully implemented by B-9089 and lines 27-34 already describe the active adapter/generated-token/derived-ppid chain. Reframe D as a regression repair to the shipped adapter/fallback behavior, identify the precise missing Codex task/agent propagation, and require a canonical contract update/new decision if taskIdentity+agentOrRoleIdentity changes the existing single-session-id semantics. Severity medium: the stale implementation status obscures whether the workstream is bug repair or a new identity-policy change.

Coverage evidence for all 10 intents passes, but the coverage reviewer cannot persist a no-blocker pass under the configured shadow routing mode: generic-token truncation/cutoff tie makes review_pass_set enforce a full-scan escalation, and rerouting with fullScanReason expands candidateSpecSet from 8 documents to the entire 130-file corpus. This reproduces the execution plan C3/mode-consistency failure and makes a documentation-only coverage pass disproportionate. Evidence: review_pass_set rejected with ranking_affecting_query_truncation + candidate_cutoff_tie; candidate_spec_route full scan returned fullScan=true and the full corpus despite candidateSpecRouting.mode=shadow. WHY: reviewer writer behavior contradicts shadow-mode advisory semantics and blocks proportionate assurance.
